title: Lab pendulum by a window, PHYS124 (real footage)

narration.transcript: I'll just measure from the pivot point down there and it looks like it's about 27 inches.

caveats: bob is small, dark and blurry with low resolution
supporting string is thin and low contrast against wall
hand briefly enters frame and perturbs swing

slow_motion.evidence: no caption or narration indicates slow motion; motion looks real-time

stated_facts.said: I'll just measure from the pivot point down there and it looks like it's about 27 inches.

observation.what_happens: A small dark bob on a long thin string swings side to side below a shelf against a white wall. It keeps swinging throughout the clip, with a hand briefly entering from the right to perturb it.

tracking.noun: pendulum bob (pointed out by Muse Spark)

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

pivot.why: the swing covers only 25° of arc; under 25° the path doesn't determine the radius (±13 px), so L isn't measured from it

given: pendulum length = 27 inch (“I'll just measure from the pivot point down there and it looks like it's about 27 inches.”)
pendulum length L = 0.6858 m (stated): hold L fixed and measure g
reasoning: Angle oscillates +/-0.22 rad with ~1.6 s period matching L=0.686 m on Earth and stays near constant amplitude with only slight decay, so L is fixed and g is fitted. Candidates go from lossless small-angle textbook to full-sin with linear viscous vs quadratic air drag to test what tiny dissipation best extends to unseen frames.

law.title: Small-angle ideal pendulum
law.summary: Tiny swing with no friction, like a perfect playground swing that never slows down.

fitted.title: Small-angle ideal pendulum
fitted.summary: Tiny swing with no friction, like a perfect playground swing that never slows down.

candidates.ifItWins: The swing is linear and lossless over 10 s; g follows from T=2*pi*sqrt(L/g) with L fixed.

law.title: Pendulum with quadratic air drag
law.summary: Air pushes back much harder when the bob moves fast, like riding a bike into wind.

fitted.title: Pendulum with quadratic air drag
fitted.summary: Air pushes back much harder when the bob moves fast, like riding a bike into wind.

candidates.ifItWins: Dissipation is aerodynamic drag proportional to speed squared; amplitude-dependent decay beats linear friction.

law.title: Damped pendulum with viscous drag
law.summary: A real swing with air slowing it gently in proportion to how fast it moves.

params.name: gamma

fitted.title: Damped pendulum with viscous drag
fitted.summary: A real swing with air slowing it gently in proportion to how fast it moves.

params.name: gamma
params.meaning: linear viscous damping rate from air and pivot

candidates.ifItWins: The tiny decay is viscous air friction proportional to speed; g is corrected for damping and large-angle sin shape.

law.title: Textbook pendulum (small angles)
law.summary: Swings like a simple harmonic oscillator: angular acceleration proportional to the angle.

fitted.title: Textbook pendulum (small angles)
fitted.summary: Swings like a simple harmonic oscillator: angular acceleration proportional to the angle.

caveats: All fitted laws sit several noise units to one side, so the noise level looks underestimated or the angle zero is off.
Drag terms fit near zero with uncertainty spanning zero, so air barely matters here.
String length was held fixed from a rough tape measure, so gravity inherits that tape error.
A brief hand nudge occurs in the clip and is not modeled as an event.
critique.finding: The swing holds steady timing set by gravity pulling with g = {g} on a string of length {L}. The misses sit a little high but show no wave or drift, so it captures the motion.
critique.headline: The bob swings as an ideal small-angle pendulum.
critique.why_it_won: It nails the swing period from the measured string without extra drag, while the free-timing version wanders off beat and drag adds nothing but wobble.

headline: The bob swings as an ideal small-angle pendulum.
finding: The swing holds steady timing set by gravity pulling with g = about 9.7 m/s² on a string of length 0.686 m (given). The misses sit a little high but show no wave or drift, so it captures the motion.

eyeball.confidence: low - crude visual period estimate with stated 27 inch length
eyeball.law_in_words: For small amplitudes the simple pendulum period is T equals 2 pi times square root of L divided by g, so g equals 4 pi squared times L divided by T squared, with L about 27 inches and T estimated by counting swings over the 300 frames at 18.7 frames per second.

clockCheck.why: Clock checked: gravity came out within 0.81% of Earth’s, so the clip plays in real time.
